HTTP/2: Don't pass the close promise to a deferred close (#17955)

Motivation:

During a graceful shutdown, `Http2ConnectionHandler` stores the caller's
close promise and later calls `ctx.close(promise)`. If the promise was
completed in between, for example because a subclass threw from
`close(...)` and the pipeline failed it, this throws "promise already
done". Since #17683 the exception is only logged, and the channel is
never closed.

Modification:

Close with a new promise and notify the caller's promise with
`PromiseNotifier.cascade(false, ...)`, like `SslHandler` does. Add a
test with a subclass whose `close(...)` throws.

Result:

The graceful shutdown always closes the Maurer","email":"norman_maurer@apple.com","date":"2026-10-21T06:43:52Z"},"committer":{"name":"GitHub","email":"noreply@github.com","date":"2026-10-21T06:43:52Z"},"message":"Verify toolchain downloads in release Dockerfiles against pinned SHA-256 (#17935) (#17940)

Motivation:

The Dockerfiles used to build the native transports bootstrapped their
toolchains via `curl ... | bash` / `curl ... | sh` (SDKMAN! and rustup)
and an unverified `wget` of the ARM GCC tarball. HTTPS was the only
integrity control, so a compromised or MitM'd download endpoint during a
build could inject a backdoored compiler into the produced native
libraries.

Modifications:

- Download the SDKMAN! installer to a file, verify it against a pinned
  SHA-256 and only then execute it (centos6, centos7, al2023,
  cross_compile_aarch64).
- Replace `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh` with a pinned rustup-init
  version that is verified against its SHA-256 (centos7, al2023,
  cross_compile_aarch64).
- Verify the ARM GCC tarball against a SHA-256 before extracting it
  (cross_compile_aarch64).
- Add docker/update-sdkman-sha.sh to refresh (or --check) the pinned
  SDKMAN! installer hash, as SDKMAN! does not version the script, and
  document it in docker/README.md.

Result:

Modified toolchain downloads are rejected at build time instead of being
executed. The SDKMAN! installer hash needs to be refreshed when SDKMAN!
changes the script.
